description: Agrarian quotations for Good Earth. The tradition of the land as a way of life and a school of character — classical husbandry, distributism, and the American agrarian line. Every entry is a quotation whose wording and attribution are checkable; where a line could not be verified it was left out rather than approximated, because a misattributed quote is worse than a shorter list.

quotes.text: If more of us valued food and cheer and song above hoarded gold, it would be a merrier world.
quotes.author: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit

quotes.text: I am in fact a Hobbit in all but size. I like gardens, trees and unmechanized farmlands.
quotes.author: J.R.R. Tolkien, Letters

quotes.text: He that breaks a thing to find out what it is has left the path of wisdom.
quotes.author: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings

quotes.text: Too much capitalism does not mean too many capitalists, but too few capitalists.
quotes.author: G.K. Chesterton, The Uses of Diversity

quotes.text: The most terribly important things must be left to ordinary men themselves.
quotes.author: G.K. Chesterton, What's Wrong with the World

quotes.text: There is no such thing on earth as an uninteresting subject; the only thing that can exist is an uninterested person.
quotes.author: G.K. Chesterton, Heretics

quotes.text: Those who labour in the earth are the chosen people of God, if ever He had a chosen people.
quotes.author: Thomas Jefferson, Notes on the State of Virginia

quotes.text: Agriculture is our wisest pursuit, because it will in the end contribute most to real wealth, good morals, and happiness.
quotes.author: Thomas Jefferson, letter to George Washington

quotes.text: O fortunate farmers, excessively fortunate, if only they knew their own blessings!
quotes.author: Virgil, Georgics

quotes.text: Observe the seasons, and do each thing in its own time.
quotes.author: Hesiod, Works and Days

quotes.text: When men are rightly occupied, their amusement grows out of their work.
quotes.author: John Ruskin, The Stones of Venice

quotes.text: Farming is the mother and nurse of the other arts, for when farming goes well all the other arts flourish.
quotes.author: Xenophon, Oeconomicus

quotes.text: No race can prosper till it learns that there is as much dignity in tilling a field as in writing a poem.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington, Up From Slavery

quotes.text: Farming looks mighty easy when your plow is a pencil and you're a thousand miles from the corn field.
quotes.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower

quotes.text: Eating is an agricultural act.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry, The Pleasures of Eating

quotes.text: The soil is the great connector of lives, the source and destination of all.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry, The Unsettling of America

quotes.text: A good farmer is one who does the work well and leaves the place better than he found it.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry, Bringing It to the Table

quotes.text: To forget how to dig the earth and to tend the soil is to forget ourselves.
quotes.author: Mohandas K. Gandhi

quotes.text: The discovery of agriculture was the first big step toward a civilized life.
quotes.author: Arthur Keith

quotes.text: The farmer has to be an optimist or he wouldn't still be a farmer.
quotes.author: Will Rogers

quotes.text: The ultimate goal of farming is not the growing of crops, but the cultivation and perfection of human beings.
quotes.author: Masanobu Fukuoka, The One-Straw Revolution

quotes.text: Cultivators of the earth are the most valuable citizens. They are the most vigorous, the most independent, the most virtuous.
quotes.author: Thomas Jefferson, letter to John Jay
